title: Etale-origin comparison intertwines compact-support projection maps
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(j,p_f)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].
Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $V_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact derived comparison [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_f=Rp_{f,\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ for ordinary etale compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $P_f=Rp_{f,\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For a bounded-below etale complex $B$, let
$$C_B:P_fV_XB\xrightarrow{\sim}V_YF_fB$$
be the canonical comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Let $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $H\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and assume $H$ has finite Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Use ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and the corresponding pro-etale tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Let $\operatorname{PF}^{e}_{M,H}:F_fM\otimes_A^LH\to F_f(M\otimes_A^Lf^*H)$ be the compactification composite of the proper counit-defined projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the canonical ordinary etale open-extension tensor comparison [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], and let $\operatorname{PF}^{p}$ be the pro-etale compactification projection map of [def-exchange-projection]. Then
$$C_{M\otimes_A^Lf^*H}\circ\operatorname{PF}^{p}_{V_XM,V_YH}
=V_Y(\operatorname{PF}^{e}_{M,H})\circ t_{F_fM,H}\circ(C_M\otimes1),$$
where $t_{B,H}:V_YB\otimes_A^LV_YH\xrightarrow{\sim}V_Y(B\otimes_A^LH)$ is the inverse of the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. On the left the target of $\operatorname{PF}^{p}$ is identified with $P_fV_X(M\otimes_A^Lf^*H)$ through [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and this same tensor comparison. The open part of $C$ uses the canonical site comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], extended termwise to complexes by exactness. The equality is natural in $M,H$ and uses the specified comparisons at the fixed compactification; it is an equality of derived morphisms. It asserts no smoothness or exceptional-pullback formula.

proof.text: Write $Z=\overline X$, $p=p_f$, $R_e=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and $R_p=Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}$. The ring $A$ is finite and commutative by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $p$ is qcqs by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Fix a lower bound $r$ for $M$ and a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $H$. By [lem-kun-0f1m], $H$ has a K-flat flat-term model supported in degrees $\geq a$, whose pullbacks along $p$ and $f$ remain K-flat with flat terms and the same termwise lower bound. Testing those models against degree-zero sheaves shows that $p^*H$ and $f^*H$ have lower Tor bound $a$. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $E=j_!^eM$ bounded below by $r$. Apply [lem-kun-derived-tensor-t-est] to obtain lower bound $a+r$ for $Q=E\otimes_A^Lp^*H$ and $D=M\otimes_A^Lf^*H$. Thus $E,Q,j_!^eD$ are bounded below. These are exactly the inputs for the direct-image comparisons used below. No finite Tor condition on $M$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F1M, lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude; morphisms.tex Tag 01W1, definition-proper; bounded-below typing for the Tag 0E48 square

proof.text: Use the tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. They identify $V_Zp_e^*H$ with $p_p^*V_YH$ and $V_Xf_e^*H$ with $f_p^*V_YH$. Their compatibility with tensor and with $j^*p^*=f^*$ can be checked on the flat-term K-flat models provided by the tensor lemma: both composites take a pulled-back pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to the same $x\otimes y$. In bidegree $(i,q)$ both use differential $dx\otimes y+(-1)^ix\otimes dy$. Hence the chain maps, and therefore their images in the derived categories, agree. We suppress these specified identifications in the next three steps. The direction $t_{B,H}$ of the question is the inverse of this lemma's pullback/tensor map.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, flat-term K-flat construction; proetale.tex comparison morphism square

proof.text:
For a bounded-below etale complex $N$ on $Z$, write $b_N:V_YR_eN\xrightarrow{\sim}R_pV_ZN$ for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Its normalization is
$$\varepsilon^p_{V_ZN}\circ p_p^*(b_N)\circ a_{R_eN}=V_Z(\varepsilon^e_N),$$
where $a:V_Zp_e^*\cong p_p^*V_Y$ is the specified pullback comparison. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the commutative square with vertical maps $p_e,p_p$ and horizontal maps $\nu_Z,\nu_Y$, with input $E=j_!^eM$ and tensor factor $H$. Its exchange is precisely $b$: both are the mate of $a^{-1}$ with the normalization just displayed. Its projection maps are the counit-defined ones of [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-exchange-projection]. This gives, under Step 2's tensor identifications,
$$b_Q\circ V_Y(\pi^e_{E,H})=\pi^p_{V_ZE,V_YH}\circ(b_E\otimes1).$$
The coherence lemma permits any commutative ringed-topos square; it does not require the site-comparison square to be Cartesian. Both components of $b$ are invertible by Step 1 and the canonical-mate lemma.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, specialized to the etale/pro-etale comparison square; equation-projection-formula-map

proof.text:
Let $e_B:V_Zj_!^eB\cong j_!^pV_XB$ be [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], applied degreewise. The two extensions are exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], so this natural chain isomorphism preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to the derived categories. Write $\gamma_e:Q\cong j_!^eD$ for [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], and $\gamma_p$ for the canonical pro-etale open tensor map. Then
$$e_D\circ V_Z(\gamma_e)=\gamma_p\circ(e_M\otimes1).$$
Here is the check of the named maps. The source is an object extended by zero, using $V_Z(\gamma_e)$ and $e_D$. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], pro-etale extension by zero is fully faithful on derived categories, so equality of these maps is detected by restriction to $X$. The comparison $e$ is the adjoint open comparison: under the open units its restriction is the identity. The restricted $\gamma_p$ is the identity by the same normalization lemma. The restricted $\gamma_e$ is also the identity: its defining sheaf tensor identity sends $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$, and the same holds in each summand of the K-flat total tensor used to define its derived map. Thus both restrictions are the same tensor/pullback identification of Step 2. Full faithfulness proves the displayed square. This uses arbitrary $M$, without a local-freeness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison (the adjoint comparison); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor

proof.text:
The fixed-compactification comparison in [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] is
$$B_B=R_p(e_B)\circ b_{j_!^eB}:V_YF_fB\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fV_XB.$$
It uses exactly the counit-mate proper comparison and the adjoint open comparison fixed above, so its inverse is $C_B$ of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] with identity etale-origin witness. This identifies the specified comparison, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism with its endpoints. By [def-exchange-projection] and the definition of the etale projection map in the statement,
$$\operatorname{PF}^e=R_e(\gamma_e)\pi^e,\qquad\operatorname{PF}^p=R_p(\gamma_p)\pi^p.$$
For $B=M,D$ the comparisons are defined and invertible by Step 1. None of this uses compactification independence or an exceptional adjunction.

source.place: First paragraph, “Because the map is obtained by transposing”: fixed-compactification normalization of the comparison used for the projection map

proof.text:
Paste Steps 3 and 4. Keeping $t=t_{F_fM,H}$ explicit, naturality of $b$ at $\gamma_e:Q\to j_!^eD$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
 B_DV_Y(\operatorname{PF}^e)
 &=R_p(e_DV_Z\gamma_e)\,b_Q\,V_Y\pi^e\\
 &=R_p\bigl(\gamma_p(e_M\otimes1)\bigr)\,\pi^p_{V_ZE,V_YH}\,(b_E\otimes1)\,t^{-1}\\
 &=\operatorname{PF}^p_{V_XM,V_YH}\,(B_M\otimes1)\,t^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is naturality of the specified direct-image mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The second uses the two proved squares. The third is naturality of the pro-etale counit-defined projection map in its first argument, followed by the compactification formula [def-exchange-projection]. It moves $R_p(e_M)$ into the first projection input; its composite with $b_E$ is exactly $B_M$. All three lines have source $V_Y(F_fM\otimes_A^LH)$ and target $P_fV_XD$. Thus this is an equality of the actual derived morphisms.

source.place: First paragraph, “Because the map is obtained by transposing”: pasting the proper and open projection squares at the chosen compactification

proof.text:
Precompose Step 6 by $t\circ(C_M\otimes1)$ and postcompose by $C_D=B_D^{-1}$. Since $(B_M\otimes1)(C_M\otimes1)=1$ and $t^{-1}t=1$, the result is precisely
$$C_D\circ\operatorname{PF}^p_{V_XM,V_YH}=V_Y(\operatorname{PF}^e_{M,H})\circ t_{F_fM,H}\circ(C_M\otimes1).$$
The target identification is Step 2's tensor comparison followed by the pullback comparison, as required. Naturality in $M,H$ follows by composing the natural transformations in Steps 2–6 and their natural inverses. For $M=0$, $H=0$ or $X=\emptyset$ these equations reduce to the unique maps between zero objects. For $j=\mathrm{id}$ the open square disappears; for $p=\mathrm{id}$ the proper square disappears. These checks require neither smoothness nor an exceptional-pullback formula.

split_report.summary: Seven-step split with no new nodes. Checks bounded-below comparison domains using the Tor hypothesis on H alone, applies ringed-topos projection/exchange coherence to the proper part, verifies the open tensor square by restriction and full faithfulness, and pastes/cancels the specified comparisons.
